bullets.title: Meditation Plus Running as a Treatment for Depression
bullets.creator: Gretchen Reynolds
bullets.note:
meditation + running might be better for anti-depressive effects than either
separately. I’m planning on testing this using an ergometer (rower).  
  
Someone I’m following on Twitter —  
[@NeilHimself](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wI4&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=r&)
— Ah, Neil Gaiman, one of my favorite polymath writing wizards. From [The
Sandman](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wIw&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=Z&)
and [American
Gods](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wId&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=2&)
to
[Coraline](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wIe&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=x&)
and [The Graveyard
Book](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wIb&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=T&),
he never ceases to impress. Fingers crossed and praying to my Lucky Charms—one
day I’ll have this fine gent on [the
podcast](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wI1&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=D&).
In the meantime, his [wonderful commencement
speech](http://www.fourhournewsletter.com/click.html?x=a62e&lc=wIt&mc=e&s=bomwH&u=w&y=W&)
might be your perfect Gaiman-land gateway drug.

bullets.title: Black Mirror
bullets.note:
(series) — This series has been a continuous “you must watch this”
recommendation from very smart friends in tech. Last week, I started binge
watching, and I devoured every episode within three days. Think of it as The
Twilight Zone meets our tech future, including the good, bad, and ugly. The
eeriest and most compelling part of this show—none of the “crazy” scenarios
are that hard to imagine being reality within the next 10-15 years. These
things are coming. If you only have time for one episode, "Be Right Back” is
solid.
